nvd.description:
Why is Microsoft republishing a CVE from 2013?
We are republishing CVE-2013-3900 in the Security Update Guide to update the Security Updates table and to inform customers that the EnableCertPaddingCheck is available in all currently supported versions of Windows 10 and Windows 11. While the format is different from the original CVE published in 2013, except for clarifications about how to configure the EnableCertPaddingCheck registry value, the information herein remains unchanged from the original text published on December 10, 2013,
Microsoft does not plan to enforce the stricter verification behavior as a default functionality on supported releases of Microsoft Windows. This behavior remains available as an opt-in feature via reg key setting, and is available on supported editions of Windows released since December 10, 2013. This includes all currently supported versions of Windows 10 and Windows 11. The supporting code for this reg key was incorporated at the time of release for Windows 10 and Windows 11, so no security update is required; however, the reg key must be set. See the Security Updates table for the list of affected software.
Vulnerability Description
A remote code execution vulnerability exists in the way that the WinVerifyTrust function handles Windows Authenticode signature verification for portable executable (PE) files. An anonymous attacker could exploit the vulnerability by modifying an existing signed executable file to leverage unverified portions of the file in such a way as to add malicious code to the file without invalidating the signature. An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could take complete control of an affected system. An attacker could then install programs; view, change, or delete data; or create new accounts with full user rights.
If a user is logged on with administrative user rights, an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could take complete control of an affected system. An attacker could then install programs; view, change, or delete data; or create new accounts with full user rights. Users whose accounts are configured to have fewer user rights on the system could be less impacted than users who operate with administrative user rights.

nvd.description:
An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists in Windows when the Windows kernel-mode driver fails to properly handle objects in memory. An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could run arbitrary code in kernel mode. An attacker could then install programs; view, change, or delete data; or create new accounts with full user rights.
To exploit this vulnerability, an attacker would first have to log on to the system. An attacker could then run a specially crafted application that could exploit the vulnerability and take control of an affected system.
The update addresses this vulnerability by correcting how the Windows kernel-mode driver handles objects in memory.

nvd.description: Multiple ZyXEL network-attached storage (NAS) devices running firmware version 5.21 contain a pre-authentication command injection vulnerability, which may allow a remote, unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on a vulnerable device. ZyXEL NAS devices achieve authentication by using the weblogin.cgi CGI executable. This program fails to properly sanitize the username parameter that is passed to it. If the username parameter contains certain characters, it can allow command injection with the privileges of the web server that runs on the ZyXEL device. Although the web server does not run as the root user, ZyXEL devices include a setuid utility that can be leveraged to run any command with root privileges. As such, it should be assumed that exploitation of this vulnerability can lead to remote code execution with root privileges. By sending a specially-crafted HTTP POST or GET request to a vulnerable ZyXEL device, a remote, unauthenticated attacker may be able to execute arbitrary code on the device. This may happen by directly connecting to a device if it is directly exposed to an attacker. However, there are ways to trigger such crafted requests even if an attacker does not have direct connectivity to a vulnerable devices. For example, simply visiting a website can result in the compromise of any ZyXEL device that is reachable from the client system. Affected products include: NAS326 before firmware V5.21(AAZF.7)C0 NAS520 before firmware V5.21(AASZ.3)C0 NAS540 before firmware V5.21(AATB.4)C0 NAS542 before firmware V5.21(ABAG.4)C0 ZyXEL has made firmware updates available for NAS326, NAS520, NAS540, and NAS542 devices. Affected models that are end-of-support: NSA210, NSA220, NSA220+, NSA221, NSA310, NSA310S, NSA320, NSA320S, NSA325 and NSA325v2

nvd.description: Strapi through 4.5.5 allows attackers (with access to the admin panel) to discover sensitive user details by exploiting the query filter. The attacker can filter users by columns that contain sensitive information and infer a value from API responses. If the attacker has super admin access, then this can be exploited to discover the password hash and password reset token of all users. If the attacker has admin panel access to an account with permission to access the username and email of API users with a lower privileged role (e.g., Editor or Author), then this can be exploited to discover sensitive information for all API users but not other admin accounts.

You can greatly reduce the risk of this issue by restricting access to the management web interface to only trusted internal IP addresses according to our recommended  best practices deployment guidelines https://live.paloaltonetworks.com/t5/community-blogs/tips-amp-tricks-how-to-secure-the-management-access-of-your-palo/ba-p/464431 .

nvd.description:
A vulnerability in the VPN web server of Cisco Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Cisco Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD) Software could allow an authenticated, remote attacker to execute arbitrary code on an affected device.
 This vulnerability is due to improper validation of user-supplied input in HTTP(S) requests. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary code as root, possibly resulting in the complete compromise of the affected device.

context: Cisco IOS and IOS XE contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) subsystem that could allow for denial of service or remote code execution. A successful exploit could allow a low-privileged attacker to cause the affected system to reload, resulting in a DoS condition, or allow a high-privileged attacker to execute arbitrary code as the root user and obtain full control of the affected system.

cisa_kev.title: Cisco IOS and IOS XE Software SNMP Denial of Service and Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
cisa_kev.description: Cisco IOS and IOS XE contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) subsystem that could allow for denial of service or remote code execution. A successful exploit could allow a low-privileged attacker to cause the affected system to reload, resulting in a DoS condition, or allow a high-privileged attacker to execute arbitrary code as the root user and obtain full control of the affected system.
cisa_kev.required_action: Apply mitigations per vendor instructions, follow applicable BOD 22-01 guidance for cloud services, or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable.

nvd.description:
A vulnerability in the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) subsystem of Cisco IOS Software and Cisco IOS XE Software could allow the following:
  An authenticated, remote attacker with low privileges could cause a denial of service (DoS) condition on an affected device that is running Cisco IOS Software or Cisco IOS XE Software. To cause the DoS, the attacker must have the SNMPv2c or earlier read-only community string or valid SNMPv3 user credentials.  An authenticated, remote attacker with high privileges could execute code as the root user on an affected device that is running Cisco IOS XE Software. To execute code as the root user, the attacker must have the SNMPv1 or v2c read-only community string or valid SNMPv3 user credentials and administrative or privilege 15 credentials on the affected device.   An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted SNMP packet to an affected device over IPv4 or IPv6 networks. 
 This vulnerability is due to a stack overflow condition in the SNMP subsystem of the affected software. A successful exploit could allow a low-privileged attacker to cause the affected system to reload, resulting in a DoS condition, or allow a high-privileged attacker to execute arbitrary code as the root user and obtain full control of the affected system.
 Note: This vulnerability affects all versions of SNMP.

nvd.description:
Update: On November 5, 2025, Cisco became aware of a new attack variant against devices running Cisco Secure ASA Software or Cisco Secure FTD Software releases that are affected by CVE-2025-20333 and CVE-2025-20362. This attack can cause unpatched devices to unexpectedly reload, leading to denial of service (DoS) conditions. Cisco strongly recommends that all customers upgrade to the fixed software releases that are listed in the Fixed Software ["#fs"] section of this advisory.
 A vulnerability in the VPN web server of Cisco Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Cisco Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD) Software could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to access restricted URL endpoints that are related to remote access VPN that should otherwise be inaccessible without authentication.

An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted HTTP requests to a targeted web server on a device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to access a restricted URL without authentication.

nvd.description: Langflow versions up to and including 1.6.9 contain a chained vulnerability that enables account takeover and remote code execution. An overly permissive CORS configuration (allow_origins='*' with allow_credentials=True) combined with a refresh token cookie configured as SameSite=None allows a malicious webpage to perform cross-origin requests that include credentials and successfully call the refresh endpoint. An attacker-controlled origin can therefore obtain fresh access_token / refresh_token pairs for a victim session. Obtained tokens permit access to authenticated endpoints — including built-in code-execution functionality — allowing the attacker to execute arbitrary code and achieve full system compromise.

nvd.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

posix-cpu-timers: fix race between handle_posix_cpu_timers() and posix_cpu_timer_del()

If an exiting non-autoreaping task has already passed exit_notify() and
calls handle_posix_cpu_timers() from IRQ, it can be reaped by its parent
or debugger right after unlock_task_sighand().

If a concurrent posix_cpu_timer_del() runs at that moment, it won't be
able to detect timer->it.cpu.firing != 0: cpu_timer_task_rcu() and/or
lock_task_sighand() will fail.

Add the tsk->exit_state check into run_posix_cpu_timers() to fix this.

This fix is not needed if CONFIG_POSIX_CPU_TIMERS_TASK_WORK=y, because
exit_task_work() is called before exit_notify(). But the check still
makes sense, task_work_add(&tsk->posix_cputimers_work.work) will fail
anyway in this case.

nvd.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tls: fix handling of zero-length records on the rx_list

Each recvmsg() call must process either
 - only contiguous DATA records (any number of them)
 - one non-DATA record

If the next record has different type than what has already been
processed we break out of the main processing loop. If the record
has already been decrypted (which may be the case for TLS 1.3 where
we don't know type until decryption) we queue the pending record
to the rx_list. Next recvmsg() will pick it up from there.

Queuing the skb to rx_list after zero-copy decrypt is not possible,
since in that case we decrypted directly to the user space buffer,
and we don't have an skb to queue (darg.skb points to the ciphertext
skb for access to metadata like length).

Only data records are allowed zero-copy, and we break the processing
loop after each non-data record. So we should never zero-copy and
then find out that the record type has changed. The corner case
we missed is when the initial record comes from rx_list, and it's
zero length.

nvd.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

crypto: af_alg - Disallow concurrent writes in af_alg_sendmsg

Issuing two writes to the same af_alg socket is bogus as the
data will be interleaved in an unpredictable fashion.  Furthermore,
concurrent writes may create inconsistencies in the internal
socket state.

Disallow this by adding a new ctx->write field that indiciates
exclusive ownership for writing.

nvd.description: Git is a fast, scalable, distributed revision control system with an unusually rich command set that provides both high-level operations and full access to internals. When reading a config value, Git strips any trailing carriage return and line feed (CRLF). When writing a config entry, values with a trailing CR are not quoted, causing the CR to be lost when the config is later read. When initializing a submodule, if the submodule path contains a trailing CR, the altered path is read resulting in the submodule being checked out to an incorrect location. If a symlink exists that points the altered path to the submodule hooks directory, and the submodule contains an executable post-checkout hook, the script may be unintentionally executed after checkout. This vulnerability is fixed in v2.43.7, v2.44.4, v2.45.4, v2.46.4, v2.47.3, v2.48.2, v2.49.1, and v2.50.1.

cisa_kev.notes: Check for signs of potential compromise on all internet accessible REACT instances after applying mitigations. nvd.description: A pre-authentication remote code execution vulnerability exists in React Server Components versions 19.0.0, 19.1.0, 19.1.1, and 19.2.0 including the following packages: react-server-dom-parcel, react-server-dom-turbopack, and react-server-dom-webpack. nvd.description: GeoServer is an open source server that allows users to share and edit geospatial data. From version 2.26.0 to before 2.26.2 and before 2.25.6, an XML External Entity (XXE) vulnerability was identified. The application accepts XML input through a specific endpoint /geoserver/wms operation GetMap. However, this input is not sufficiently sanitized or restricted, allowing an attacker to define external entities within the XML request. This issue has been patched in GeoServer 2.25.6, GeoServer 2.26.3, and GeoServer 2.27.0.

nvd.description: Ray is an AI compute engine. Prior to version 2.52.0, developers working with Ray as a development tool can be exploited via a critical RCE vulnerability exploitable via Firefox and Safari. This vulnerability is due to an insufficient guard against browser-based attacks, as the current defense uses the User-Agent header starting with the string "Mozilla" as a defense mechanism. This defense is insufficient as the fetch specification allows the User-Agent header to be modified. Combined with a DNS rebinding attack against the browser, and this vulnerability is exploitable against a developer running Ray who inadvertently visits a malicious website, or is served a malicious advertisement (malvertising). This issue has been patched in version 2.52.0.

nvd.description: n8n is an open source workflow automation platform. Versions starting with 0.211.0 and prior to 1.120.4, 1.121.1, and 1.122.0 contain a critical Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability in their workflow expression evaluation system. Under certain conditions, expressions supplied by authenticated users during workflow configuration may be evaluated in an execution context that is not sufficiently isolated from the underlying runtime. An authenticated attacker could abuse this behavior to execute arbitrary code with the privileges of the n8n process. Successful exploitation may lead to full compromise of the affected instance, including unauthorized access to sensitive data, modification of workflows, and execution of system-level operations. This issue has been fixed in versions 1.120.4, 1.121.1, and 1.122.0. Users are strongly advised to upgrade to a patched version, which introduces additional safeguards to restrict expression evaluation. If upgrading is not immediately possible, administrators should consider the following temporary mitigations: Limit workflow creation and editing permissions to fully trusted users only; and/or deploy n8n in a hardened environment with restricted operating system privileges and network access to reduce the impact of potential exploitation. These workarounds do not fully eliminate the risk and should only be used as short-term measures.

nvd.description:
A buffer overflow vulnerability in the User-ID™ Authentication Portal (aka Captive Portal) service of Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS software allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code with root privileges on the PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls by sending specially crafted packets. 

The risk of this issue is greatly reduced if you secure access to the User-ID™ Authentication Portal per the  best practice guidelines https://knowledgebase.paloaltonetworks.com/KCSArticleDetail  by restricting access to only trusted internal IP addresses.

Prisma Access, Cloud NGFW and Panorama appliances are not impacted by this vulnerability.

The security risk posed by this issue is minimized by restricting access to the management interface to only trusted internal IP addresses according to our recommended  best practice deployment guidelines https://live.paloaltonetworks.com/t5/community-blogs/tips-amp-tricks-how-to-secure-the-management-access-of-your-palo/ba-p/464431 .



This issue is applicable to PAN-OS software on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and on Panorama (virtual and M-Series).



Cloud NGFW and Prisma® Access are not impacted by this vulnerability.

context: Zammad GmbH Zammad contains an improper privilege management vulnerability that can allow the local zammad user to escalate privileges to root. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-102489.

nvd.description: Zammad packages built with packager.io (DEB and RPM) could have allowed a local attacker who already had file system write privileges as the unprivileged zammad service account to escalate to full root privileges on the host. Service processes began running as root and executed files that were owned and writable by the zammad account before dropping their identity to that account. An attacker holding that foothold could have escalated within seconds, because the affected services were restarted automatically whenever they stopped; no administrator interaction was required. Only installations from the DEB and RPM packages were affected — installations from source or the official container images were not. All released packaged versions were affected.

nvd.description: GPUStack is an open-source GPU cluster manager for AI model serving and GPU instance provisioning. Prior to 2.2.0, get_current_user in gpustack/api/auth.py treated a loopback request source as the built-in administrator when force_auth_localhost was false, which was the default. A remote request could appear to originate from 127.0.0.1 because client_ip_getter accepted a same-host reverse proxy peer or a client-supplied X-GPUStack-Real-IP loopback value. The bypass allowed unauthenticated administrative access, including user and model changes, persistent administrator API-key creation, disclosure of worker and cloud-provider secrets, and code execution through POST /v2/inference-backends/from-yaml. Exploitation was observed in the wild against a 2.1.1 deployment. This issue is fixed in version 2.2.0.

nvd.description: PHP uses longjmp() for out-of-memory (OOM) errors to exit the current context and abort handling of the request. Some contexts may not properly account for this scenario and leave request memory in an uninitialized state before performing an allocation. The subsequent request cleanup procedure may read or branch on this memory. Multiple OOM strategies can consistently trigger this condition and lead to remote code execution (RCE).

nvd.description: PHP has various global state that temporarily points into request memory. In some scenarios, global state may not be correctly reset, or may be repopulated after being reset. The global state may then refer to request memory even after it has been freed. Subsequent requests may read or branch on this stale state before it is fully initialized. Multiple strategies can trigger this condition and produce remote code execution (RCE).

nvd.description: FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. Prior to 1.11.3, sofia_presence_handle_sip_i_message() split the To user of an inbound SIP MESSAGE on a plus sign and treated the left side as a chat protocol selector. Selecting the api chat proto reached switch_api_execute(), allowing a peer whose MESSAGE was accepted to run FreeSWITCH API commands, including operating-system command sinks, with the daemon's privileges. Inbound chat is enabled on the stock internal and external profiles, and any authenticated profile account is sufficient; stock directory users without password material can also remove that barrier in affected configurations. The flaw permits configuration and credential disclosure, arbitrary call control, and command execution, and exploitation has been observed in the wild. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.3.

nvd.description:
Deserialization of Untrusted Data in Apache Roller versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code. The XML-RPC endpoint accepts vendor extension types and deserializes them before authenticating the requester.

This is the same vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384, which listed only Apache Roller 6.1.5 as affected. This issue is being actively exploited.

Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later, which disables the extension types and rejects XML-RPC requests when the XML-RPC feature is disabled.

Users who cannot upgrade right away should set "enabledForExtensions" to "false" in WEB-INF/web.xml, or remove the "/roller-services/xmlrpc" servlet mapping, and restart Roller. Disabling XML-RPC in the administration UI is not enough, because older versions deserialize the request before checking that setting.

Prior to 6.9.2 and 6.10.1, REST cookie parsing turns authenticationToken=j:%7B%7D into {}. REST authentication passes that object to the XO token provider without requiring a string. The token collection treats {} as an unfiltered lookup and returns its first token; the provider authenticates as that token's owner if it is unexpired. The authenticated /rest/v0/users/me/authentication_tokens route then returns reusable login token IDs. This vulnerability is actively exploited in the wild. This vulnerability is fixed in 6.9.2 and 6.10.1.

This vulnerability is due to improper input validation for specific HTTP requests. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted HTTP request to an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to write files to the underlying operating system that could be used later to elevate to root.
Note: Cisco has assigned this security advisory a Security Impact Rating (SIR) of Critical rather than High as the score indicates. The reason is that exploitation of this vulnerability could result in an attacker elevating privileges to root.
Note: To exploit this vulnerability, the WebDialer service must be enabled. WebDialer is disabled by default.

nvd.description: This is a vulnerability in Bitbucket Data Center, Confluence Data Center, Jira Service Management Data Center, Jira Software Data Center, Bamboo Data Center. Crowd Data Center, Crucible and Fisheye. This Arbitrary File Access vulnerability allows an unauthenticated attacker to access specific files within the web application root directory in affected versions. Exploitation requires prior knowledge of the target file's exact name and path; this vulnerability does not allow attackers to enumerate or list directory contents. In some configurations, there may be some sensitive files that make this highly severe. This vulnerability allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to access specific files within the web application root directory in affected versions. The vulnerability must be addressed for affected versions of: -- Bitbucket Data Center, introduced in version >= 4.6.0, fix versions: 9.4.26, 10.2.8, 10.5.1 -- Confluence Data Center, introduced in version >= 5.10.0, fix versions 9.2.26, 10.2.19 -- Crowd Data Center, introduced in version >= 2.11.0, fix versions 6.3.7, 7.0.3, 7.1.7, 7.2.4 -- Jira Software Data Center, introduced in version >= 7.1.0, fix versions 9.12.40, 10.3.26, 11.3.12 -- Jira Service Management Data Center, introduced in version >= 3.1.0, fix versions 5.12.40, 10.3.26, 11.3.12 -- Bamboo Data Center >= 7.0.1, fix versions 10.2.24, 12.1.12 -- Crucible, fix versions 4.9.15 -- Fisheye, fix version 4.9.15 -- Exploitation requires prior knowledge of the target file's exact name and path. The vulnerability does not include the capability to enumerate or list directory contents.

nvd.description:
Improper Input Validation, Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection') vulnerability in Apache ActiveMQ Broker, Apache ActiveMQ.

Apache ActiveMQ Classic exposes the Jolokia JMX-HTTP bridge at /api/jolokia/ on the web console. The default Jolokia access policy permits exec operations on all ActiveMQ MBeans (org.apache.activemq:*), including
BrokerService.addNetworkConnector(String) and BrokerService.addConnector(String).

An authenticated attacker can invoke these operations with a crafted discovery URI that triggers the VM transport's brokerConfig parameter to load a remote Spring XML application context using ResourceXmlApplicationContext.
Because Spring's ResourceXmlApplicationContext instantiates all singleton beans before the BrokerService validates the configuration, arbitrary code execution occurs on the broker's JVM through bean factory methods such as Runtime.exec().



This issue affects Apache ActiveMQ Broker: before 5.19.4, from 6.0.0 before 6.2.3; Apache ActiveMQ All: before 5.19.4, from 6.0.0 before 6.2.3; Apache ActiveMQ: before 5.19.4, from 6.0.0 before 6.2.3.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 5.19.4 or 6.2.3, which fixes the issue

nvd.description: LiteLLM is a proxy server (AI Gateway) to call LLM APIs in OpenAI (or native) format. From version 1.81.16 to before version 1.83.7, a database query used during proxy API key checks mixed the caller-supplied key value into the query text instead of passing it as a separate parameter. An unauthenticated attacker could send a specially crafted Authorization header to any LLM API route (for example POST /chat/completions) and reach this query through the proxy's error-handling path. nvd.description: LiteLLM is a proxy server (AI Gateway) to call LLM APIs in OpenAI (or native) format. From version 1.74.2 to before version 1.83.7, two endpoints used to preview an MCP server before saving it — POST /mcp-rest/test/connection and POST /mcp-rest/test/tools/list — accepted a full server configuration in the request body, including the command, args, and env fields used by the stdio transport. When called with a stdio configuration, the endpoints attempted to connect, which spawned the supplied command as a subprocess on the proxy host with the privileges of the proxy process. The endpoints were gated only by a valid proxy API key, with no role check. Any authenticated user — including holders of low-privilege internal-user keys — could therefore run arbitrary commands on the host. This issue has been patched in version 1.83.7.

nvd.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: skbuff: preserve shared-frag marker during coalescing

skb_try_coalesce() can attach paged frags from @from to @to.  If @from
has SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG set, the resulting @to skb can contain the same
externally-owned or page-cache-backed frags, but the shared-frag marker
is currently lost.

That breaks the invariant relied on by later in-place writers.  In
particular, ESP input checks skb_has_shared_frag() before deciding
whether an uncloned nonlinear skb can skip skb_cow_data().  If TCP
receive coalescing has moved shared frags into an unmarked skb, ESP can
see skb_has_shared_frag() as false and decrypt in place over page-cache
backed frags.

Propagate SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG when skb_try_coalesce() transfers paged
frags.  The tailroom copy path does not need the marker because it copies
bytes into @to's linear data rather than transferring frag descriptors.

nvd.description: LiteSpeed User-End cPanel Plugin before 2.4.5 allows privilege escalation (possibly to root), as exploited in the wild in May 2026. The recommended minimum version is 2.4.7.

nvd.description: Starlette is a lightweight ASGI framework/toolkit. Prior to version 1.0.1, the HTTP `Host` request header was not validated before being used to reconstruct `request.url`. Because the routing algorithm relies on the raw HTTP path while `request.url` is rebuilt from the `Host` header, a malformed header could make `request.url.path` differ from the path that was actually requested. Middleware and endpoints that apply security restrictions based on `request.url` (rather than the raw `scope` path) could therefore be bypassed. Users should upgrade to a version greater than or equal to version 1.0.1, which validates the `Host` header against the grammar of RFC 9112 §3.2 / RFC 3986 §3.2.2 when constructing `request.url` and falls back to `scope["server"]` for malformed values.

nvd.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

netfilter: bridge: make ebt_snat ARP rewrite writable

The ebtables SNAT target keeps the Ethernet source address rewrite
behind skb_ensure_writable(skb, 0).  This is intentional: at the bridge
ebtables hooks the Ethernet header is addressed through
skb_mac_header()/eth_hdr(), while skb->data points at the Ethernet
payload.  Asking skb_ensure_writable() for ETH_HLEN bytes would check
the payload, not the Ethernet header, and would reintroduce the small
packet regression fixed by commit 63137bc5882a.

However, the optional ARP sender hardware address rewrite is different.
It writes through skb_store_bits() at an offset relative to skb->data:

        skb_store_bits(skb, sizeof(struct arphdr), info->mac, ETH_ALEN)

skb_header_pointer() only safely reads the ARP header; it does not make
the later sender hardware address range writable.  If that range is
still held in a nonlinear skb fragment backed by a splice-imported file
page, skb_store_bits() maps the frag page and copies the new MAC address
directly into it.

Ensure the ARP SHA range is writable before reading the ARP header and
before calling skb_store_bits().

nvd.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv6: account for fraggap on the paged allocation path

In __ip6_append_data(), when the paged-allocation branch is taken
(MSG_MORE / NETIF_F_SG / large fraglen), alloclen and pagedlen are
computed as

	alloclen = fragheaderlen + transhdrlen;
	pagedlen = datalen - transhdrlen;

datalen already includes fraggap (datalen = length + fraggap). When
fraggap is non-zero, this is not the first skb and transhdrlen is zero.
The fraggap bytes carried over from the previous skb are copied just past
the fragment headers in the new skb's linear area. The linear area is
therefore undersized by fraggap bytes while pagedlen is overstated by the
same amount, and the copy writes past skb->end into the trailing
skb_shared_info.

An unprivileged user can trigger this via a UDPv6 socket using
MSG_MORE together with MSG_SPLICE_PAGES.

The bad accounting was introduced by commit 773ba4fe9104 ("ipv6:
avoid partial copy for zc"). Before commit ce650a166335 ("udp6: Fix
__ip6_append_data()'s handling of MSG_SPLICE_PAGES"), the negative
copy value caused -EINVAL to be returned. That later commit allowed
MSG_SPLICE_PAGES to proceed in this case, making the corruption
triggerable.

The non-paged branch sets alloclen to fraglen, which already accounts
for fraggap because datalen does. Bring the paged branch in line by
adding fraggap to alloclen and subtracting it from pagedlen.

After this adjustment, copy no longer collapses to -fraggap on the
paged path, so remove the stale comment describing that old arithmetic.
Since a negative copy is no longer expected for a valid MSG_SPLICE_PAGES
case, remove the MSG_SPLICE_PAGES exception from the negative copy check.

context: MikroTik RouterOS contains a missing authentication for critical function vulnerability which allows kernel memory disclosure and denial of service in the btest service.

cisa_kev.title: MikroTik RouterOS Missing Authentication for Critical Function Vulnerability
cisa_kev.description: MikroTik RouterOS contains a missing authentication for critical function vulnerability which allows kernel memory disclosure and denial of service in the btest service.
cisa_kev.required_action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.

nvd.description:
RouterOS accepts a "related" btest connection before the corresponding primary session has completed authentication. An unauthenticated client can use this state to start an IPv4 UDP test. With "random-data=false", the sender transmits an uninitialized tail from a kernel packet buffer. A separate unchecked, inverted packet-size interval causes unsigned integer underflow, anomalously large fragmented output, and can restart the RouterOS kernel.



This issue was fixed in versions: 6.49.21 (Long-term), 7.23.4 (Long-term) and 7.24.2 (Stable)

context: Arista Extensible Operating System (EOS) contains an incomplete comparison with missing factors vulnerability when the switch incorrectly decapsulate and forwards other unexpected tunneled packet with a destination IP matching its configured decapsulation IP.

cisa_kev.title: Arista Extensible Operating System Incomplete Comparison with Missing Factors Vulnerability
cisa_kev.description: Arista Extensible Operating System (EOS) contains an incomplete comparison with missing factors vulnerability when the switch incorrectly decapsulate and forwards other unexpected tunneled packet with a destination IP matching its configured decapsulation IP.
cisa_kev.required_action: Apply mitigations per vendor instructions, follow applicable BOD 22-01 guidance for cloud services, or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable.

nvd.description:
On affected platforms running Arista EOS where a tunnel decapsulation configuration—such as VXLAN (Virtual Extensible LAN), decap-groups, or a GRE (Generic Routing Encapsulation) tunnel interface—is present, the switch will incorrectly decapsulate and forward other unexpected tunneled packet with a destination IP matching its configured decapsulation IP. This occurs because the switch does not verify the tunnel protocol type, potentially leading to the unexpected processing of non-configured tunnel traffic.



This issue has been reported as being exploited in the wild.

nvd.description:
A vulnerability in the database service feature of Cisco Expressway Series could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker with network access to a Cisco Expressway device to execute arbitrary operating system commands as root.

This vulnerability is due to the use of persistent cookies. Additionally, there is insufficient validation of client certificates when the TLS Verify Mode is set to Enabled for clustering, which means that client certificates are not validated. An attacker with possession of the cookies could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to the database service and invoking specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary commands as root on the underlying operating system of an affected device.
Note: Cisco Expressway Series refers to Cisco Expressway Core (Expressway-C) devices and Cisco Expressway Edge (Expressway-E) devices.

nvd.description:
** UNSUPPORTED WHEN ASSIGNED ** Deserialization of an inbound SOAP fault in Apache Axis 1.x allows unauthenticated remote class instantiation. When a SOAP <Fault> carries a <detail><exceptionName> element, Axis loads the named class and, if a String <data> element is also present, instantiates it through its String constructor before checking that it is an AxisFault. Loading alone runs the class's static initializer. With a suitable class on the application's classpath this leads to remote code execution. The fault is parsed while the engine resolves the target service, before any per-service handler chain runs, so authentication handlers configured on a service do not protect against it. This affects all Apache Axis 1.x versions through 1.4.



As Axis 1 has been EOL we recommend you migrate to a different SOAP engine, such as Apache Axis 2/Java. Alternatively you could use a build of Axis with the patch from https://github.com/apache/axis-axis1-java/commit/41f3b4e8d04e310ca81f86b92630ab2c11d608bd applied. The Apache Axis project does not expect to create an Axis 1.x release fixing this problem.

context:
Crypt::JWT versions before 0.024 for Perl skip issuer, subject, audience and JWT ID checks when the claim is absent or the option is a plain string.

decode_jwt runs the verify_iss, verify_sub, verify_aud and verify_jti checks only when the token carries the claim, and honours an option only as a Regexp or CODE reference. Any other value, such as verify_aud => 'myapp', is ignored.

An application that relies on these checks accepts a validly signed token meant for a different issuer, subject or audience.

context:
WWW::Form::UrlEncoded::XS versions before 0.27 for Perl read one byte before the input buffer when parsing an empty string.

parse_urlencoded and parse_urlencoded_arrayref check for a trailing "&" or ";" by reading the last byte of the input, without first checking that the input has any bytes.

A remote client that sends an empty query string or request body to an application parsing it with this module can crash the process.

nvd.description:
WWW::Form::UrlEncoded::XS versions before 0.27 for Perl read one byte before the input buffer when parsing an empty string.

parse_urlencoded and parse_urlencoded_arrayref check for a trailing "&" or ";" by reading the last byte of the input, without first checking that the input has any bytes.

A remote client that sends an empty query string or request body to an application parsing it with this module can crash the process.

context:
WWW::Form::UrlEncoded::XS versions before 0.28 for Perl write past the end of the Perl argument stack when parse_urlencoded returns many pairs.

parse_urlencoded returns its result as a list, pushing each decoded key and value onto the argument stack without first extending the stack to fit them. parse_urlencoded_arrayref returns an array reference and is not affected.

A remote client that sends a query string or request body with many pairs to an application parsing it with parse_urlencoded can corrupt memory and crash the process.

nvd.description:

context:
Application Performance Management 9.60 patch versions before IP4 are affected. This issue seems to be present throughout the application, as several endpoints or functionalities that are restricted to Admin users can be directly accessed by Regular users. The authorization method of the application can be bypassed allowing users to perform unauthorized actions to their role. The application supports different levels of access. The application performs authorization checks to keep users from accessing functionality outside of their role such as create, verify, and/or repair. 




This authorization method can be bypassed. During VA testing, it was found that under the User Reports inside the Applications menu, it is possible to  create links and different reports. However, the creation of custom links, Excel reports, and service reports are restricted to admin users. Hence, it is possible for regular users with the least privileges to directly access these 

pages and the application allows them to further use these restricted functionalities.

nvd.description:
Application Performance Management 9.60 patch versions before IP4 are affected. This issue seems to be present throughout the application, as several endpoints or functionalities that are restricted to Admin users can be directly accessed by Regular users. The authorization method of the application can be bypassed allowing users to perform unauthorized actions to their role. The application supports different levels of access. The application performs authorization checks to keep users from accessing functionality outside of their role such as create, verify, and/or repair. 




This authorization method can be bypassed. During VA testing, it was found that under the User Reports inside the Applications menu, it is possible to  create links and different reports. However, the creation of custom links, Excel reports, and service reports are restricted to admin users. Hence, it is possible for regular users with the least privileges to directly access these 

pages and the application allows them to further use these restricted functionalities.

context:
In Application Performance Management versions before 9.60 IP4, The application is vulnerable to cross-site scripting wherein the application does not properly validate the input parameters, allowing scripts to be injected and then executed in the context of a user’s browser. This can lead to the attacker stealing sensitive information, impersonating users, or performing actions on their behalf.  Also, the application may also be vulnerable to the below attacks:

• Link Injection – This occurs when an attacker inserts a malicious link into a webpage, often in a way that makes it appear legitimate. When user clicks on the link, they may be directed to a harmful website or prompted to download malicious files.



• Frame Injection – This attack involved embedding a webpage within an invisible frame on another site, User interacts with what appears to be a legitimate site, but their actions are performed on the malicious page, potentially leading to unintended actions or data theft.

nvd.description:
In Application Performance Management versions before 9.60 IP4, The application is vulnerable to cross-site scripting wherein the application does not properly validate the input parameters, allowing scripts to be injected and then executed in the context of a user’s browser. This can lead to the attacker stealing sensitive information, impersonating users, or performing actions on their behalf.  Also, the application may also be vulnerable to the below attacks:

• Link Injection – This occurs when an attacker inserts a malicious link into a webpage, often in a way that makes it appear legitimate. When user clicks on the link, they may be directed to a harmful website or prompted to download malicious files.



• Frame Injection – This attack involved embedding a webpage within an invisible frame on another site, User interacts with what appears to be a legitimate site, but their actions are performed on the malicious page, potentially leading to unintended actions or data theft.

context:
z_impl_pwm_capture_cycles() in drivers/pwm/pwm_capture.c stores its capture context (struct z_pwm_capture_cb_data, including a struct k_sem) on its own stack and registers a pointer to it as the driver capture callback's user_data. When called with a K_NO_WAIT timeout, k_sem_take() returns -EBUSY, which the function did not handle: it fell through, returned the uninitialized status field, copied uninitialized period/pulse values to the caller when that status happened to be zero, and returned without disabling the capture or clearing the callback.

pwm_capture_cycles() is a system call, and z_vrfy_pwm_capture_cycles() passes the caller's timeout through unchanged. With CONFIG_USERSPACE and CONFIG_PWM_CAPTURE enabled, an unprivileged user-mode thread that has been granted access to a capture-capable PWM device can pass K_NO_WAIT to trigger the defect. Without userspace the function is only reachable from trusted application code.

The uninitialized values come from the thread's privileged (kernel) stack, so a user-mode caller can read up to 8 bytes of stale kernel stack memory per call. More seriously, when the capture later completes, the driver ISR invokes z_pwm_capture_cycles_callback() with the dangling pointer. The callback writes into the expired kernel stack region and calls k_sem_give() on whatever memory now occupies it, which can corrupt live kernel stack frames and make the scheduler walk a forged wait queue. The result is kernel memory corruption from interrupt context, leading at least to a crash and possibly to privilege escalation out of the userspace sandbox. The fix rejects K_NO_WAIT with -EINVAL before any capture is configured.

context:
The Grow R502-A fingerprint sensor driver (drivers/sensor/grow_r502a/grow_r502a.c) points drv_data->rx_buf.data at an rx_packet buffer on the caller's stack and enables the UART RX interrupt before waiting 1500 ms for a reply. When the wait timed out, transceive_packet() returned -ETIMEDOUT but left the RX interrupt enabled and rx_buf.data still pointing at the caller's buffer.

Once the caller's frame has returned, any bytes that arrive late on the UART are written by the interrupt handler uart_cb_handler() through the dangling pointer into stack memory that the thread has since reused. The bytes come from the device on the other end of the UART. An attacker with physical access who replaces or impersonates the fingerprint module can trigger this by delaying a reply past the timeout and then sending a packet. A slow or faulty genuine module can also trigger it by accident.

The result is a write of attacker-chosen bytes into a live thread stack. The write length comes from the header of the late packet. Commit 96968fac22b, which landed together with this fix, bounds it to a header plus CONFIG_R502A_DATA_PKT_SIZE bytes; affected releases do not have that bound. This can crash the device and may allow control-flow hijacking, depending on what occupies the reused stack region. The fix disables the RX interrupt, resets the RX semaphore and clears rx_buf.data on timeout, and the interrupt handler now refuses to write when no receive buffer is armed.

context:
The Grow R502-A fingerprint sensor driver (drivers/sensor/grow_r502a/grow_r502a.c) receives sensor responses in the UART interrupt handler uart_cb_handler(). Once the 9-byte header has arrived, the handler reads the 16-bit package length from the header and uses it as the byte count for further uart_fifo_read() calls into rx_buf.data. It never checks that length against the destination buffer. That buffer is a union r502a_packet on the calling thread's stack, set up by transceive_packet(), and is only CONFIG_R502A_DATA_PKT_SIZE + 12 bytes long (140 bytes by default).

A malicious or counterfeit sensor module, or an attacker who tampers with the UART wiring, can reply to any driver command with a header that declares a length of up to 65535 bytes. context:
In Eclipse Che versions 7.61.0 through 7.124.0 three related defects in the SCM-OAuth flow, chain into a Medium-severity finding:



1. Open redirect (CWE-601) — `EmbeddedOAuthAPI.callback()` and the OAuth1 callback issue `307 Temporary Redirect` to whatever URL was carried in the `redirect_after_login` field of the OAuth `state` parameter. The value is fully attacker-controlled and never compared against an allow-list of permitted hosts.



2. Missing CSRF nonce in OAuth `state` (CWE-352) — `OAuthAuthenticator.prepareState()` builds the `state` parameter solely by URL-encoding the original request's query string. No random nonce is bound to the user's session, so an attacker can pre-compute a callback URL carrying _their own_ SCM authorization `code` and have a logged-in victim open it. `callback()` then stores the attacker's SCM token under the victim's Che identity (`personalAccessTokenManager.store(...)`).



3. Mutable field on a `@Singleton` (CWE-362 / CWE-488) — `EmbeddedOAuthAPI` is `@Singleton` but stores the per-request `redirect_after_login` value into the instance field `private String redirectAfterLogin`. Any user's `authenticate()` call overwrites the field for all concurrent users; the `access_denied` error-path of `callback()` then redirects to the _last writer's_ URL.

  *  None of the source plugins in the buildstream, buildstream-plugins or buildstream-plugins-community repositories use the vulnerable `open_file` method

Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer vulnerability in the AArch64 JIT in Erlang OTP erts allows an attacker to crash the BEAM virtual machine via input that reaches a chained integer range guard, such as an oversized numeric character reference parsed by xmerl_sax_parser.

In erts/emulator/beam/jit/arm/instr_common.cpp, BeamModuleAssembler::emit_is_ge_lt wraps its generated code in preserve_cache and marks only TMP1 as clobbered. When the compared value is not a small integer, the generated code calls the shared fragment is_ge_lt_shared, which also overwrites ARG1 and other caller-saved registers. The register cache keeps stale entries, so later instructions may use a clobbered register as an Erlang term and the emulator dies with a segmentation fault. A reference such as &#576460752303423488; takes this path in the ?is_char guard of the SAX parser. Only AArch64 builds that run the JIT are affected. The x86-64 JIT and interpreter builds do not contain the faulty code.

This issue affects OTP from OTP 27.0 before OTP 27.3.4.20, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.1.3, corresponding to erts from 15.0 before 15.2.7.15, 16.4.0.8, and 17.1.2.

Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input vulnerability in the BER decoder in Erlang/OTP snmp allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust CPU via an SNMP message that contains an OBJECT IDENTIFIER with a very long sub-identifier.

snmp_pdus:dec_oid_element/3 does not limit the number of base-128 octets in a sub-identifier, and snmp_pdus:dec_oid_elements/3 does not limit the number of sub-identifiers, so one sub-identifier can span the whole datagram. When the value exceeds the native integer size, each further octet copies a growing bignum, and decoding time grows quadratically with the sub-identifier length. The agent and the manager decode OIDs before they check community strings or SNMPv3 credentials, inside the single network interface process (snmpa_net_if or snmpm_net_if). That process does not read the next datagram until decoding completes.

This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.20, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.1.3, corresponding to snmp from 4.25.1 before 5.18.2.3, 5.20.2.4, and 5.20.7. Whether OTP before OTP 17.0, corresponding to snmp before 4.25.1, is affected is unknown.

Out-of-bounds Write vulnerability in the external term format decoder in Erlang OTP erts allows an attacker who controls the input to binary_to_term/1,2 to abort the Erlang VM via a NEWER_REFERENCE_EXT term with a zero-length ID. decoded_size in erts/emulator/beam/external.c accepts a reference whose 16-bit Len field is zero, but dec_term always reads one ID word. dec_term then runs 4 bytes ahead of the position that decoded_size validated. It decodes the bytes that follow as terms that were never sized, and writes past the reserved process heap.

The abort takes down every process on the node. Supervision, try/catch and the safe option do not prevent it. enif_binary_to_term() and the distribution protocol reach the same decoder, and distribution is assumed to run on trusted networks only. NEW_REFERENCE_EXT also accepts a zero length, but its range check on the first ID word rejects the shifted input. On 32-bit builds, a zero-length reference of either type at the end of the input, followed by trailing bytes, can write one word past the reserved heap.

This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.20, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.1.3, corresponding to erts from 6.0 before 15.2.7.15, 16.4.0.8, and 17.1.2. Whether OTP before OTP 17.0, corresponding to erts before 6.0, is affected is unknown.

Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers ('HTTP Request/Response Splitting') vulnerability in Erlang OTP inets (httpc module) allows HTTP Request Splitting.

httpc writes request header names and values to the wire without neutralizing CR, LF or NUL characters. On the default path http_request:mk_key_value_str/2, and with the headers_as_is option httpc_request:http_headers/2, build each header line by plain concatenation of the name, ": ", the value and CRLF. A CR/LF in a name or value ends the header line early. An attacker who controls data that an application puts into a header passed to httpc:request/4,5 can add or override request headers, or append a second request on the same connection.

Applications that pass only constant or validated header names and values are not affected. The request line is not affected, because uri_string rejects URLs that contain raw CR/LF.

This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.20, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.1.3, corresponding to inets from 5.10 before 9.3.2.9, 9.6.2.5, and 9.8.2. Whether OTP before OTP 17.0, corresponding to inets before 5.10, is affected is unknown.

Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in Erlang OTP inets (httpd_script_env module) allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust the atom table of an httpd server that serves ESI scripts.

When mod_esi builds the environment for an ESI callback, httpd_script_env:http_env_element/3 checks that a request header name already exists as an atom, then creates the atom http_<header-name> with list_to_atom/1. Atoms are never garbage collected, and each new atom passes the existence check on a later request. So a header named node creates http_node, a header named http_node creates http_http_node, and so on. A stream of requests to any ESI URL grows the atom table until it reaches its limit (+t), and then the whole Erlang VM aborts, together with every application on the node.

This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.20, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.1.3, corresponding to inets from 5.10 before 9.3.2.9, 9.6.2.5, and 9.8.2. Whether OTP before OTP 17.0, corresponding to inets before 5.10, is affected is unknown.

context:
Uncontrolled Recursion vulnerability in the external term format decoder in Erlang OTP erts allows an attacker who controls the input to binary_to_term/1,2 to abort the Erlang VM via a fun term with funs nested in its integer fields. dec_term in erts/emulator/beam/external.c decodes terms iteratively, except for the OldIndex and OldUniq fields of NEW_FUN_EXT and the Arity field of EXPORT_EXT. For these fields it calls itself, and it checks that the result is a small integer only after the call returns. An input that places another fun in such a field, nested to sufficient depth, recurses once per level, exhausts the stack of the scheduler thread and crashes the VM. The input must be large enough to reach that depth.

The abort takes down every process on the node. Supervision, try/catch and the safe option do not prevent it. enif_binary_to_term() and the distribution protocol reach the same decoder, and distribution is assumed to run on trusted networks only.

This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.20, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.1.3, corresponding to erts from 6.0 before 15.2.7.15, 16.4.0.8, and 17.1.2. Whether OTP before OTP 17.0, corresponding to erts before 6.0, is affected is unknown.

context:
Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in lasp-lang partisan allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to abort the Erlang VM of a node via Excessive Allocation. partisan_peer_service_server:handle_info/2 decodes every frame that arrives on the peer listener with binary_to_term/1, without the safe option, before handle_inbound/2 interprets the message and before any peer authentication takes place. TLS is off by default and the listener accepts connections from any host, so one frame that names more atoms than the atom table holds aborts the VM. partisan_peer_service_client:handle_info/2 decodes frames from the server side of a connection the same way.

The decode also materializes funs, ports and references the frame encodes and inflates compressed terms. The demonstrated impact is denial of service. partisan does not invoke decoded funs, so code execution was not shown.

This issue affects partisan: from 3.0.0 before 6.4.0.

Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference vulnerability in xmerl_scan in Erlang OTP xmerl allows an attacker to exhaust the memory of the Erlang VM via an XML document that names an external DTD.

With default options, xmerl_scan:string/1,2 and xmerl_scan:file/1,2 fetch and parse the external DTD named in a <!DOCTYPE root SYSTEM "..."> declaration. fetch_DTD/2 in lib/xmerl/src/xmerl_scan.erl passes every system identifier to the default fetch function, which maps file: and absolute URIs to local paths, and int_file_decl/3 then reads the whole file with file:read_file/1. This happens whether or not validation is enabled, and the allow_entities option, which is false by default since OTP 27, only governs <!ENTITY> declarations and does not stop the fetch. A document naming file:///dev/zero makes the node read without bound until the operating system kills it for lack of memory, and the parse never returns.

This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.20, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.1.3, corresponding to xmerl from 1.3.7 before 2.1.3.4, 2.1.9.1, and 2.2.1. Whether OTP before OTP 17.0, corresponding to xmerl before 1.3.7, is affected is unknown.

Improper Input Validation vulnerability in ash-project ash allows an attacker to bypass the input validation of the field types of a :keyword attribute or argument.

Ash.Type.Keyword.cast_input/2 in lib/ash/type/keyword.ex converts a map input to a keyword list in try_map_to_keyword/2, which casts each declared field with Ash.Type.cast_stored/3. That function is meant for trusted values read back from the data layer, so client input skips the cast_input/2 of each field type. apply_constraints/2 casts the result again with cast_input/2, but most types accept a value of their own type unchanged. An embedded resource field is built without its create action, so its validations and changes do not run and its non-public attributes can be set. A :function field accepts a capture string such as &Mod.fun/1, and a :term field decodes Erlang external term format.

This issue affects ash: from 3.24.0 before 3.38.1.

Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws allows an attacker who controls an S3 bucket name to send the application's signed S3 requests to a host of their choice.

With virtual_host: true, ExAws.Operation.S3.add_bucket_to_path/2 in lib/ex_aws/operation/s3.ex builds the request hostname from the bucket name and the configured host without checking the bucket name. A bucket such as attacker.example/x? turns the request URL into https://attacker.example/x?.s3.amazonaws.com/key, so the request is signed for and sent to attacker.example. The attacker receives upload bodies, the access key id and request signature, and any STS session token, and controls the response the application parses. With bucket_as_host: true the bucket is the whole hostname, so any valid hostname redirects the request.

This issue affects ex_aws: from 2.1.7 before 2.8.0.

context:
Out-of-bounds Read vulnerability in the external term format decoder in Erlang OTP erts allows an attacker who controls the input to binary_to_term/1,2 to read memory after the input, and to change one byte there, via a FLOAT_EXT term without a terminating zero byte. decoded_size in erts/emulator/beam/external.c checks only that the 31 bytes of the FLOAT_EXT field are present. dec_term then passes the field to sys_chars_to_double, which scans to a NUL byte without a length limit. When the field has no NUL, the scan continues into the bytes after the field, and those bytes change the decoded float. When the radix character is found after the field and strtod does not accept it, sys_chars_to_double overwrites that byte (a , becomes a .). The VM can fault if the scan reaches an unmapped page.

The safe option does not prevent this. enif_binary_to_term() and the distribution protocol reach the same decoder, and distribution is assumed to run on trusted networks only. The write is limited to the one radix byte. No arbitrary write or code execution was shown.

This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.20, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.1.3, corresponding to erts from 6.0 before 15.2.7.15, 16.4.0.8, and 17.1.2. Whether OTP before OTP 17.0, corresponding to erts before 6.0, is affected is unknown.

context:
Strong::Random versions through 0.96 for Perl allow every later rand output to be predicted from three earlier ones.

The generator keeps its state in a single number. Each call multiplies the state by a factor derived from it, and the returned digits encode that factor, so three consecutive outputs determine the state however the generator was seeded. Outputs are also biased: the first digit after the decimal point is never zero, so rand(256) never returns 1 to 24.

An attacker who sees three consecutive outputs can predict the tokens, passwords or key bytes that the same object later issues to other users.

context:
Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature vulnerability in Erlang OTP ssl (ssl_handshake module) allows an on-path attacker to impersonate any server to a TLS 1.2 or DTLS client.

When a server sends no Certificate message and a ServerKeyExchange without a signature, ssl_handshake:decode_server_key/3 reports the signature algorithm as anon, and ssl_handshake:verify_signature/5 returns true for anon without a public key. The client does not require a certificate for a certificate-authenticated key exchange, so the handshake completes for the ecdhe_rsa, ecdhe_ecdsa, dhe_rsa and dhe_dss key exchanges with a cipher suite the client offered. Certificate path validation, verify_fun and the hostname check do not run, and ssl:connect/3 returns {ok, Socket} with {verify, verify_peer} set. The TLS 1.3 client is not affected.

This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.14, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.0.3, corresponding to ssl from 5.3.4 before 11.2.12.10, 11.6.0.8, and 11.7.3.

context:
The shell command ACL for the feature scope (etc/org.apache.karaf.command.acl.feature.cfg) restricts feature:install, feature:uninstall, feature:start and feature:stop to the admin role, but had no entry for feature:requirement-add or feature:requirement-remove.

The provisioning resolver turns a requirement into the same install/start (or uninstall) action as feature:install / feature:uninstall: a bundle: requirement causes an arbitrary bundle to be downloaded and started, and a feature: requirement installs that feature. Because the two commands had no ACL, a user authenticated with only the viewer (and ssh) role could invoke them and cause Apache Karaf to download, install and start an attacker-chosen bundle, which then runs with the full authority of the Karaf process — thereby bypassing the admin-only authorization enforced on feature:install and bundle:install.

This is the same class of issue as the feature:repo-add -i / feature:repo-remove -u bypass, on sibling commands not covered by that earlier fix.Mitigation:Upgrade to Apache Karaf 4.4.12 or 4.5.0 (or later), which restrict feature:requirement-add and feature:requirement-remove to the admin role.

As an interim workaround on affected versions, add the following two lines to etc/org.apache.karaf.command.acl.feature.cfg; the change is picked up at runtime without a restart:

requirement-add = admin

requirement-remove = admin

context: A **NULL pointer dereference** flaw has been found in the acl_check_dns_host_name() and acl_validate_spn_value() functions in source4/dsdb/samdb/ldb_modules/acl.c of the Active Directory domain controller ACL module in the **Samba** package. The checks read the account name after a request that removes it, and they do not test that the value is present. A low-privileged network attacker or user who can update the DNS host name or service principal name of their own computer account can include a removal of sAMAccountName in that same LDAP modify. The directory process crashes. Repeating the modify keeps the directory service unavailable.

nvd.description: A **NULL pointer dereference** flaw has been found in the acl_check_dns_host_name() and acl_validate_spn_value() functions in source4/dsdb/samdb/ldb_modules/acl.c of the Active Directory domain controller ACL module in the **Samba** package. The checks read the account name after a request that removes it, and they do not test that the value is present. A low-privileged network attacker or user who can update the DNS host name or service principal name of their own computer account can include a removal of sAMAccountName in that same LDAP modify. The directory process crashes. Repeating the modify keeps the directory service unavailable.

context:
Use After Free vulnerability in Erlang/OTP erts allows an attacker who can create a file system entry with a chosen name to hang or abort the Erlang VM on macOS.

On macOS, the VM decodes file names with do_utf8_to_list_normalize in erts/emulator/beam/erl_unicode.c. When a name starts with a combining mark, such as U+0301, cleanup_norm builds the first list cells but does not return its advanced heap pointer. The caller then releases the heap words that hold those cells, and the returned list refers to released process heap memory that the next allocation overwrites. file:list_dir/1, file:list_dir_all/1, file:del_dir_r/1 and filelib:wildcard/1 on a directory that contains such a name do not return, and the VM does not stop on SIGTERM. file:read_link/1 on a symbolic link with such a target aborts the VM with size_object: bad tag. Only loss of availability was demonstrated.

This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.20, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.1.3, corresponding to erts from 6.0 before 15.2.7.15, 16.4.0.8, and 17.1.2.

context:
Incorrect authorization in affected versions of network-manager in Ubuntu allows a local attacker with code execution as the whoopsie user to invoke root-restricted D-Bus methods via an Ubuntu-specific D-Bus policy, disrupting network connectivity or altering network configuration.

  An Ubuntu-specific D-Bus policy configuration in NetworkManager granted the whoopsie user unrestricted send access to org.freedesktop.NetworkManager, overriding the default deny-list for root-only methods (SetLogging, Sleep, LoadConnections, and ReloadConnections). A local attacker able to execute code as the whoopsie user could exploit this to disrupt system networking or alter NetworkManager logging and connection configurations.

nvd.description:
Incorrect authorization in affected versions of network-manager in Ubuntu allows a local attacker with code execution as the whoopsie user to invoke root-restricted D-Bus methods via an Ubuntu-specific D-Bus policy, disrupting network connectivity or altering network configuration.

A local attacker able to execute code as the whoopsie user could exploit this to disrupt system networking or alter NetworkManager logging and connection configurations.

context: AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.6.41 through 0.11.1, the OAuth provider endpoints check a calling application's client secret against a scrypt hash synchronously on the REST API event loop. Anyone who knows the client ID of an active confidential OAuth application can stall the REST API for all users by sending a stream of requests with a wrong secret. No account or token is required. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.2.

Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in the application/vnd.hex+erlang request body parser in hexpm hexpm allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute operating system commands via a crafted Erlang external term format request body. This vulnerability was actively exploited against the hex.pm service on 2026-11-23.

HexpmWeb.ErlangFormat.decode/1 in lib/hexpm_web/erlang_format.ex decodes the body with Plug.Crypto.non_executable_binary_to_term/2, which accepts maps that have a __struct__ key. HexpmWeb.PlugParser.parse/5 returns the decoded term as the request params. The parser runs in the endpoint before routing and authentication, so a POST to any route reaches it. Elixir dispatches protocols on the __struct__ key, so the client selects which Inspect and Enumerable implementations run when error reporting inspects the params. A chain through Ecto.Query.DynamicExpr and DBConnection.Stream reaches an apply/3 call on a {module, function, args} tuple taken from the request body.

This issue affects hex.pm: from 2016-02-23 before 2026-11-23; hexpm/hexpm: from ab1bbcef7cc8395d1056d3b1aa6a174353492d59 before 379b0a29bcc95164249f38ad7d772a37a8ff9533.

When sftpEnabled=true (the default configuration in etc/org.apache.karaf.shell.cfg), the SSH server exposes the karaf.base directory tree through the MINA SSHD SFTP subsystem and SCP command factory without verifying the authenticated user's roles beyond the initial sshRole login check. Consequently, an authenticated user with only low-privileged roles (such as viewer and ssh) can read sensitive configuration and key files (including etc/users.properties and etc/host.key) or write arbitrary bundles/configurations into monitored directories (such as deploy/ or etc/), leading to privilege escalation and arbitrary code execution.


Apache Karaf 4.4.13 and 4.5.0 introduce the sftpRole configuration property in org.apache.karaf.shell (defaulting to admin) and enforce role-based access control on SFTP subsystem creation, SCP command execution, and virtual filesystem access.

Mitigation / WorkaroundUsers are recommended to upgrade to Apache Karaf 4.4.13 or 4.5.0.




On earlier versions where SFTP/SCP access is not required, set sftpEnabled=false in etc/org.apache.karaf.shell.cfg and restart the SSH server bundle (or Karaf instance).

context: AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.6.67 to 0.11.2, organization and team billing-manager roles intended only for spend management are treated as ordinary members across workflow, run, library, and marketplace routes. Although the role matrix in autogpt_platform/autogpt_libs/autogpt_libs/auth/permissions.py withholds run access and workflow creation, those routes do not enforce the matrix and their underlying membership lookups ignore the caller's role. As a result, a team billing manager can read team workflows and other members' runs (including inputs, outputs, and per-node data), while an organization billing manager can view shared workflows and runs and create workflows and marketplace listings; neither can modify or delete other members' workflows. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.3.

Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in woylie flop allows a remote attacker to execute code on the server via a crafted pagination cursor.

Flop.Cursor.decode/2 in lib/flop/cursor.ex decodes the after and before parameters with :erlang.binary_to_term/2 in :safe mode. Its check rejects functions, PIDs, ports and references, but it accepts maps, and therefore structs of any module. Flop passes the decoded values to Ecto as query parameters. A cursor value that nests an Ecto.Query.DynamicExpr struct with a DBConnection.Stream struct as its binding fails the Ecto cast. Ecto then inspects the value for the error message, the Inspect implementation enumerates the stream, and DBConnection calls the module, function and arguments in the :log option of the stream.

This issue affects flop: from 0.8.0 before 0.26.7, from 0.27.0 before 0.27.3, from 0.28.0 before 0.28.1, and from 0.29.0 before 0.29.2.

In Apache Karaf, the default command ACL configuration for the feature scope (etc/org.apache.karaf.command.acl.feature.cfg, defined in assemblies/features/standard/src/main/feature/feature.xml and the child-instance template instance/src/main/resources/org/apache/karaf/instance/resources/etc/org.apache.karaf.command.acl.feature.cfg) restricts feature:install, feature:uninstall, feature:start, and feature:stop to users with the admin role, while leaving feature:requirement-add and feature:requirement-remove without ACL entries.


Because Karaf's command guard (SecuredSessionFactoryImpl) allows commands with no matching ACL rule (NO_MATCH) to execute, an authenticated SSH user holding only the ssh and viewer roles can execute feature:requirement-add bundle:<uri> (or feature:<name>). RequirementAdd forwards the requirement directly to FeatureService.addRequirements(), causing the resolver to download, install, and start an arbitrary bundle with the Karaf JVM process's full authority, bypassing the admin-only restrictions on feature:install and bundle:install. Similarly, feature:requirement-remove allows removing provisioning requirements and uninstalling features/bundles.

MitigationUsers are recommended to upgrade to Apache Karaf 4.4.13 or 4.5.0.




For existing deployments or upgrades that preserve existing files in etc/, add the following rules to etc/org.apache.karaf.command.acl.feature.cfg (and any child instance etc/org.apache.karaf.command.acl.feature.cfg files):




requirement-add = admin 

requirement-remove = admin

context: In Valkey before 7.2.16, 8.0.x before 8.0.13, 8.1.x before 8.1.12, 9.0.x before 9.0.8, 9.1.x before 9.1.4 and 9.2.0 release candidates, when client eviction is enabled (maxmemory-clients is not 0), an authenticated user who can write to a key that other clients are blocked on (for example with BLPOP, BLMPOP, BZPOPMIN or XREAD BLOCK) can trigger a use-after-free. While the clients blocked on that key are served, evictClients() can select and free the client whose command made the key ready, although that command is still executing, and the server then keeps using the freed client. The blocked clients do not have to belong to the attacker. The result is a reliable crash of the server process. Servers with the default maxmemory-clients 0 are not affected.

context:
XML Injection vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 allows an attacker who controls an object version id passed to ExAws.S3.delete_multiple_objects/3 to add objects to the batch delete.

delete_multiple_objects/3 in lib/ex_aws/s3.ex builds the <Delete> request body by placing each object's version between <VersionId> tags without XML escaping. A version such as v1</VersionId></Object><Object><Key>important-file</Key></Object><Object><Key>x</Key><VersionId>v2 closes the caller's object and opens new ones, so S3 deletes objects the application never listed, including other users' objects in the same bucket.

This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.0 before 2.6.0.

context: AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.6.46 through 0.11.1, AutoPilot does not remove the media files that its block runs write to the executor's disk, leading to exhaustion. A signed-in user who can use AutoPilot can grow the temporary storage used by AutoPilot's tool process by about 1 GiB per chat. Once that filesystem is full, file handling fails for every user served by that executor and for anything else writing to the same disk. No other user's data is read or changed. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.2.

context: AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. From versions 0.6.15 through 0.10.0, the value of a host-scoped credential header was exposed to other hosts via HTTP redirects. SendAuthenticatedWebRequestBlock attaches a host-scoped credential's headers to a request, but once a redirect took that request to a different origin, only three fixed header names (Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie) were removed. A host-scoped credential's header names are free-form (the UI suggests X-API-Key), so a credential carried under any other name followed the redirect to the new origin. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.

context: SeaweedFS is a distributed storage system for files and blobs. context: SeaweedFS is a distributed storage system for files and blobs. Prior to version 4.46, FileStore.ValidatePassword in the SFTP server does not reject zero-length secrets before comparing them, causing an empty login password to match any account configured without one, such as public-key-only or certificate-only users. context: Glances is an open-source system cross-platform monitoring tool. In versions prior to 4.5.7, the on-alert action command tokenizer in secure.py treats quote characters as argument boundaries without escaping. A monitored stat value, such as a mount point name, that is quoted in an action command template can contain a quote character that breaks out of its quote boundary and injects additional arguments into the process the action invokes. No shell operator is needed for this attack. This issue has been fixed in version 4.5.7.

context: OpenEXR is the reference implementation and specification for the EXR image format, widely used in the motion picture industry. From versions 3.4.0 through 3.4.18 and 3.5.0 through 3.5.2, decoding a crafted HT-compressed EXR chunk can cause ht_undo_impl() to write a 4-byte pixel value through a pointer that is not 4-byte aligned. context: CodeSafe is an open-source Python library for code encryption, decryption, and safe evaluation using Python's AST module. From versions 0.0.1 through 0.0.4, the safe_eval() function can be bypassed with indirect subscript calls such as builtins'exec', because AST validation blocks only direct calls to dangerous built-ins.
